An Explicit Family of Log-Concave Counterexamples to the Gaussian Completely Monotone Conjecture

Jiayang Zou Affiliation: Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA; jyangzou@stanford.edu Affiliation: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; {qiudao, fanluyao, gjy0515, jiawang}@sjtu.edu.cn    Luyao Fan Affiliation: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; {qiudao, fanluyao, gjy0515, jiawang}@sjtu.edu.cn    Jiayang Gao Affiliation: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; {qiudao, fanluyao, gjy0515, jiawang}@sjtu.edu.cn    Jia Wang Affiliation: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China; {qiudao, fanluyao, gjy0515, jiawang}@sjtu.edu.cn
Abstract

We construct smooth, strictly log-concave counterexamples to the Gaussian completely monotone conjecture in every dimension. In one dimension, they form an explicit family fmf_{m} whose signed mmth entropy derivative at time zero is negative for every sufficiently large mm; the inequality persists for all sufficiently small positive times. Tensorization with a broad Gaussian factor gives the higher-dimensional examples. The argument is analytic and self-contained. It reduces the sign to a two-frequency entropy calculation on the circle and transfers the resulting asymptotic to the real line through an exact heat-flow formula for Gaussian-windowed Fourier modes. The proof was developed by GPT-5.6 Sol Pro under the authors’ guidance.

I Introduction

Let Pt=et∂x2/2P_{t}=e^{t\partial_{x}^{2}/2} denote the heat semigroup on ℝ\mathbb{R}. If XX has density ff, then Pt​fP_{t}f is the density of X+t​ZX+\sqrt{t}\,Z, where ZZ is a standard Gaussian independent of XX. We consider the Boltzmann entropy profile

ℋf​(t)=∫ℝ(Pt​f)​(x)​log⁡(Pt​f)​(x)​𝑑x.\mathcal{H}_{f}(t)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}(P_{t}f)(x)\log(P_{t}f)(x)\,\,\mathrm{d}x. (1)

The Gaussian completely monotone conjecture of Cheng and Geng [1] asserts that

(−1)k​ℋf(k)​(t)≥0,k≥1,t>0.(-1)^{k}\mathcal{H}_{f}^{(k)}(t)\geq 0,\qquad k\geq 1,\quad t>0. (2)

Our heat convention corresponds to adding Gaussian noise of variance tt; the alternative convention et∂x2e^{t\partial_{x}^{2}} only rescales time.

We begin with the construction. For each integer m≥5m\geq 5, set

am=2−m/4,bm=2−m,κm=8am,a_{m}=2^{-m/4},\qquad b_{m}=2^{-m},\qquad\kappa_{m}=8a_{m}, (3)

and consider the probability density

fm(x)=Zm−1e−κmx2/2(1+amcosx+bmcos2x),x∈ℝ,f_{m}(x)=Z_{m}^{-1}e^{-\kappa_{m}x^{2}/2}\bigl(1+a_{m}\cos x+b_{m}\cos 2x\bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}, (4)

where ZmZ_{m} is the normalizing constant.

Theorem 1.

For every m≥5m\geq 5, the density fmf_{m} in (4) is smooth, strictly positive, Gaussian-decaying, and strictly log-concave. Moreover, with

β:=32​2>1,\beta:=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}>1, (5)

one has

(−1)m​ℋfm(m)​(0)=−1196​βm+o⁡(βm)(m→∞).(-1)^{m}\mathcal{H}_{f_{m}}^{(m)}(0)=-\frac{11}{96}\beta^{m}+o(\beta^{m})\qquad(m\to\infty). (6)

Consequently, for every sufficiently large mm, there is εm>0\varepsilon_{m}>0 such that

(−1)m​ℋfm(m)​(t)<0,0≤t<εm.(-1)^{m}\mathcal{H}_{f_{m}}^{(m)}(t)<0,\qquad 0\leq t<\varepsilon_{m}. (7)

Thus (2) fails for smooth strictly log-concave densities on ℝ\mathbb{R}.

Corollary 5 tensors fmf_{m} with an explicit broad Gaussian factor and gives the same asymptotic failure in every dimension.

The conjecture belongs to a hierarchy of Gaussian inequalities arising from entropy power along the heat flow. Costa proved the concavity of entropy power under Gaussian convolution [2, 3]. McKean’s Gaussian optimality conjecture asks whether the signed entropy derivatives are extremized by Gaussian distributions of the same variance [4], while Toscani proposed a third-order entropy-power inequality that helped motivate this hierarchy [5]. Wang proved that the entropy power conjecture implies McKean’s conjecture [6], and McKean’s conjecture in turn implies (2). Thus

entropy-power conjecture⟹McKean’s conjecture,McKean’s conjecture⟹GCMC.\begin{gathered}\text{entropy-power conjecture}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{McKean's conjecture},\\[-0.86108pt] \text{McKean's conjecture}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{GCMC}.\end{gathered}

Several lower-order cases of (2) were known before the recent counterexamples. Cheng and Geng proved (2) in one dimension through order four [1]. In arbitrary dimension the first two orders follow from entropy-power concavity, and the third-order inequality is known in dimensions at most four [7]. For one-dimensional log-concave inputs, Zhang, Anantharam, and Geng developed a linear-matrix-inequality method for higher entropy derivatives [8]. Wang subsequently proved (2) through order five for log-concave inputs in every dimension by higher-order Otto calculus [9].

The de Bruijn identity gives

−ℋf′​(t)=12​I​(Pt​f),I⁡(g)=∫ℝd|∇log⁡g|2​g​𝑑x,-\mathcal{H}_{f}^{\prime}(t)=\frac{1}{2}I(P_{t}f),\qquad I(g)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}|\nabla\log g|^{2}g\,\,\mathrm{d}x,

where the second formula applies to a density gg on ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}. Thus (2) is equivalent to complete monotonicity of the Fisher information profile. Since every positive completely monotone function is log-convex, GCMC would in particular imply log-convexity of t↦I⁡(Pt​f)t\mapsto I(P_{t}f). This weaker consequence already separates dimension one from higher dimensions. Ledoux, Nair, and Wang proved Fisher-information log-convexity in dimension one [10], whereas a recent hexagonal construction disproved it in every dimension d≥2d\geq 2 [11]. Thus a one-dimensional GCMC counterexample cannot be detected at the log-convexity level and must instead violate a higher-order complete-monotonicity sign.

Gu and Sellke recently found such a higher-order obstruction [12]. Their counterexample is a symmetric probability measure μ\mu supported on seventeen points. The entropy profile (1) extends to probability measures through the density of Pt​μP_{t}\mu. In our heat convention, their certified estimate reads

0.3625<ℋμ(5)​(2/3)<0.3725.\frac{0.36}{2^{5}}<\mathcal{H}_{\mu}^{(5)}(2/3)<\frac{0.37}{2^{5}}.

This is the smallest possible order of failure for unrestricted one-dimensional data, by the theorem of Cheng and Geng. Their candidate was found with GPT-5.5 Pro, and its sign was certified from an exact one-dimensional integral using SageMath/Arb ball arithmetic. The same paper also established the existence of a log-concave counterexample by heat regularization and backward propagation of complete monotonicity.

Theorem 1 gives a direct analytic construction in the log-concave class. The mmth member of the explicit family is paired with the mmth derivative, whose signed value is negative for every sufficiently large mm. An exact entropy expansion and uniform remainder estimates establish the sign without a separate numerical certificate.

Proof strategy. We first remove the Gaussian envelope and study the two-frequency factor on the circle. Expanding its entropy, we group the surviving monomials by spectral level. A term at level jj carries BjmB_{j}^{m}, where Bj=j2−j/2B_{j}=j2^{-j/2}. The unique dominant level is j=3j=3. The two terms at this level have coefficients −1/8-1/8 and 1/961/96, producing the leading constant −11/96-11/96 in (6); all other levels form a uniformly bounded remainder.

We then restore the Gaussian envelope. The exact heat evolution of a Gaussian-windowed Fourier mode reduces the real-line calculation to the periodic one, up to Fourier-filtering and time-change errors of o⁡(βm)o(\beta^{m}). The curvature contributed by the Gaussian envelope enforces strict log-concavity, and analyticity preserves the negative sign for sufficiently small positive times. Finally, Gaussian tensorization and additivity of entropy give the higher-dimensional counterexamples.

Proof of Theorem 1.

The estimates preceding Lemma 3 prove smoothness, positivity, Gaussian decay, and strict log-concavity. Lemmas 2 and 4 give

(−1)m​ℋfm(m)​(0)=−1196​βm+o⁡(βm),(-1)^{m}\mathcal{H}_{f_{m}}^{(m)}(0)=-\frac{11}{96}\beta^{m}+o(\beta^{m}),

which is negative for all sufficiently large mm.

For each such fixed mm, the exact representation (22) extends holomorphically to a neighborhood of zero. Indeed, the principal logarithm used in the filtering argument is uniformly analytic there, the spatial Fourier series converges normally, and dm​(t)d_{m}(t) stays away from zero. Thus ℋfm(m)​(t)\mathcal{H}_{f_{m}}^{(m)}(t) is right-continuous at zero, and the strict negative sign persists on some interval [0,εm)[0,\varepsilon_{m}). This proves (7). ∎
